info.description:
The versioned public surface of IOTA Hub, for scripts and agents: create an observation draft, upload its files, run the observer checks, fix or dismiss findings, submit — plus read access to events, observations and their files.

Authentication is the `X-API-Key` header alone. A key acts as its owner: it can never do or see more than that person can in the web app. There is no CORS on this surface, so keys stay out of browsers — call it from a script, not from a page.

The quickstart, error table and limits are at /developers/api; keys are managed at /developers.
info.title: IOTA Hub Public API v1

post.description:
Look up an observation by its natural identity before creating one, so a client that lost a create response (or is re-run) resumes the existing draft instead of creating a second.

`found` is `observation` when **you** already have a draft or submission for this asteroid, star, UTC date and station (the most recent if several), with its `status`, `amendment_count` and `web_url`; `event` is then its attached event, if any. Otherwise `found` is `event` when an event for that asteroid + star + date exists (its id and status only — what the Events list shows), else `none`. Another user's observation is never returned.

Text compares case-insensitively with whitespace collapsed. `asteroid_id` and `star_catalog` compare only when given; without `asteroid_id` no event lookup is made. `station` always compares: absent, null and `""` are the same station, and each station is its own observation.

event.summary: No observation of yours, but the event exists

post.summary: Check whether an observation already exists

post.description:
Create a draft observation and, in the same call, presign one upload target per declared file. POST each file straight to S3 with the returned `upload_url` and `fields`, then call `finalize`.

Identity fields (observer, asteroid, star, time, result) are not accepted: they are read from the report spreadsheet when the `report` slot is finalized.

The optional `aperture_record` slot takes a PyMovie `.pymovie` aperture record or a Tangra `.lc` file, up to 500 MB.

Declare any other file (plots, notes) with `slot: "attachment"`, repeated once per file. Attachments follow the web app's rules: at most 25 per observation, 50 MB each, and executable/script extensions are refused. Each attachment target carries the `attachment_id` it will be stored under.

parameters.description: Client-generated key making this call safe to retry. A replay returns the first call's response and does no second write. Keys expire after 24 hours.

get.description:
Fetch a single observation or draft. A draft answers only to its owner — to anyone else it is a 404, so an id can never be probed for existence.

For a draft the response is self-describing: `readiness` says what is still missing, `checks` carries the latest observer-check run (null when it has never been checked), and `next_actions` gives the stable verbs to follow next.

patch.description:
Set what the observer decides on a draft: the OWC link (`owc_link_choice` + `owc_event`), the unnumbered-asteroid confirmation, comments, and the required-files bypass. Omitted fields are unchanged. Any change starts a new check run.

The server auto-matches the OWC event itself after the report is finalized; read `owc.resolution` for the outcome. Use this call when it could not choose: `picked` takes an id from `owc.resolution.candidates`, `pasted` takes any OWC id or URL and is validated against OWC and against the report, `proceed_unlinked` records a deliberate "no link".

Stable codes: `409 stale_version`, `422 report_derived_fields` (`details.fields`), `422 owc_not_a_candidate`, `422 owc_link_unparseable`, `422 owc_link_not_found`, `422 owc_link_mismatch` (`details.violations`), `503 owc_unavailable`.

post.description:
Commit a staged upload onto the observation. Finalizing the `report` slot of a draft re-parses the workbook and rewrites the identity fields; `report_parse` says how that went.

On a **submitted** observation this is the owner's amend: it stamps `amended_at`, increments `amendment_count` and turns `status` to `amended`. A replaced report is parsed before anything is stored; one describing a different observation (asteroid, star, UTC date, result or station) is `422 identity_changed` with `details.changed`, and the observation is left exactly as it was. Once its event is in review or later the owner is refused with `409 already_processed`.

post.description:
Submit the draft: match or create its event, attach, and flip it to `submitted`. The body is optional: send `{version}` to refuse a draft that changed since you read it (`409 stale_version`), or nothing to submit the current version.

Submitting an observation that is already submitted answers **200** with its current state, so a retry after a lost response is safe.

Stable codes: `422 missing_required` (`details.missing_required`), `409 open_findings` (`details.open_findings`), `409 checks_stale`, `409 stale_version`, `409 event_files_conflict`, `422 owc_link_mismatch` (a pasted OWC link that disagrees with the report; `details.violations`). State refusals carry `details.status`, `details.observation_id` and `details.amendment_count`.

An unresolved OWC link never blocks submit — but observer check 11 is then skipped (see `checks.skipped`).

servers.description: The environment serving this document. Until the production release, only the development deployment serves the public API, and that is where third-party developers build: sign up there, create a key, and point your client at this base URL. The production base URL is published at release.

tags.description: The versioned public surface at `/public/v1`, for scripts and agents. **Authentication is the `X-API-Key` header alone** — `Authorization` and the mock-auth headers are ignored here, and there is no CORS, so keys stay out of browsers. **A key acts as its owner**: it resolves to that user's real `UserContext`, so this surface can never do or see more than the same person can in the web app, and never less on the endpoints it exposes. Least privilege comes from the surface itself — reviewer and coordinator workflow is simply not mounted here — plus the key's scopes (`observations:write` for every write, `read` for every read). The response models are frozen and additive-only within v1; every error is problem-details (`{code, message, hint, details}`) with a stable `code` to branch on, and every 429 carries `Retry-After`. Submission is collapsed for scripts: create a draft declaring its files, POST each presigned target to S3, finalize, poll the observation resource (`readiness`, `checks`, `next_actions`), then submit.
tags.name: Public API v1
